o.text: Inherited from Old Anatolian Turkish طوار (ṭavar, davar), from Proto-Turkic *tabar (“wares, goods, livestock”), whence also Russian това́р (továr, “goods”).
From Classical Persian زادگان, plural of Classical Persian زاده (as in شاه زادگان (“kingsʼ sons, princes”)).
Borrowed from Russian шампу́нь (šampúnʹ), from French shampooing, from Hindi चाँपो (cā̃po).
From Proto-Turkic *siāĺ- (“to be astonished, to slander”).
